what: Kroger is one of the largest grocers in the United States, with around 2,700 supermarkets under Kroger, Ralphs, Fred Meyer and other local names, plus pharmacies and fuel stations. Its own-brand products and retail advertising business are increasingly important.
customers: American grocery shoppers, mostly in the Midwest, South and West.
money: groceries, fresh food, own brands, pharmacy and fuel
advertising sold to suppliers using its shopper data
moat: Store density and distribution in its regions, plus own-brand products that customers cannot buy elsewhere.
risks: Net margin of about 1% leaves almost no room for error
The blocked Albertsons merger cost years of management attention and a large fee
Walmart and Costco compete hard on price
Debt of about $23 billion against very little cash
opportunities: Retail media advertising earns high margins on data it already has
Own-brand products are more profitable than national brands
Grocery demand is stable through recessions
watch: Identical-store sales excluding fuel, and digital sales growth.
